CipherBox v1 has **no production deployment** (as of 2026-07-19) — only the staging environment exists, and both desktop and web authenticate against Web3Auth **DEVNET** (free tier). MAINNET has never been used by any real identity. Production release (web or desktop) is deliberately deferred until billing revenue or investment funds Web3Auth MAINNET authentication.

**Why:** Code configs are misleading here — web maps `production → MAINNET` (`apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit.ts:6-11`) while desktop maps all envs including production to DEVNET (`apps/desktop/src/auth.ts:54-59`). This "keypair split" is latent, never-exercised prod config, not an operational issue.

**How to apply:** Don't treat production Web3Auth config paths as live or flag the desktop/web network divergence as an active bug — it's unshipped config. v2 decided a clean break on data and no identity-continuity obligation (see [[cipher-box-next-wayfinder-map]], ticket "Decide: v1 vault migration stance").
--- project-web-e2e-only-on-main-push
name: project-web-e2e-only-on-main-push
description: Web E2E does not run on PRs — only on push to main (and manual dispatch); how a regression slipped through
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa272e9e-42b1-4669-b018-72e17add5018
  modified: 2026-08-08T17:59:20.846Z

**OBSOLETE for v2 as of 2026-08-08 — the title claim no longer holds.** `ci.yml` triggers on
`pull_request: branches: [main]` and calls `web-e2e.yml` as a `workflow_call` at `ci.yml:890`, gated
on the `web` or `e2e` path filters (`ci.yml:72-76`) and behind a stable always-reporting result gate
that branch protection requires. So **Web E2E Smoke DOES run on a v2 PR** when the PR touches a path
it covers. `web-e2e.yml` itself is now `workflow_dispatch` + `workflow_call` only — it has no `push`
trigger at all. The rest of this memory is v1 history: the flake and local-confirmation techniques
below still read true, the trigger claim does not.

The `ci-e2e.yml` "CI E2E Tests" workflow triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch`. On PRs the "Web E2E" job does NOT run — PRs show only `SDK E2E Tests` + a `Verify E2E Passed` gate (which passes when web-e2e is skipped). So a web regression is first observed on the **post-merge push to main**, not on the PR.

**Why it matters:** PR #494 (phase 47 SDK folder-state/publish consolidation) broke `writable-shares.spec.ts:330` ("4.3 Alice edits Bob's file") and it passed all PR checks, then failed Web E2E on the main push. Confirm regressions by comparing the failing commit to its parent's Web E2E run (`gh run list --workflow ci-e2e.yml --branch main`).

**How to verify a web fix before merge:** push the branch and manually dispatch. Two options:

- **Web-only (faster, preferred):** `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` — `web-e2e.yml` is directly `workflow_dispatch`-enabled and checks out `ref: inputs.ref || github.sha` = the branch HEAD, so it runs the identical Web E2E job against branch code with no merge. Direct dispatch resolves repo secrets directly (no `secrets: inherit` parent needed), so it faithfully reproduces the main-push run.
- **Both web+desktop:** `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run ci-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` (dispatch forces both via the `Force all changes on manual dispatch` step). Poll the "Web E2E" job specifically.

This was the gap behind the **#498** regression (self-bootstrap folderTree clobber) too — tracked/fixed as Phase 48 REQ-1, whose acceptance gate is a pre-merge `web-e2e.yml` dispatch.

**Single-worker cascade-abort HIDES regressions (PR #555, 2026-06-24).** `playwright.config.ts` is `workers:1, fullyParallel:false, retries:0` and CI caps max-failures, so tests run sequentially in alphabetical file order and the run ABORTS after a couple failures — every later test shows "did not run". A flaky EARLY test (`invite-link-workflow` 1.1 account-creation, `journey-timing` login-to-vault, `media-preview` upload — all chronically flaky) skips the whole tail. `writable-shares` sorts LAST, so across 3 dispatches a real regression in it was repeatedly masked (the run never reached it; its discard-warning signature was absent only because the path wasn't exercised). Lesson: a web-e2e dispatch that fails on a *different* early test each run does NOT clear your test — don't infer pass from absence-in-failures. Captured as todo `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-24-web-e2e-flaky-cascade-abort.md`.

**Confirm a single spec LOCALLY when CI flakes can't reach it.** Playwright's `webServer` block auto-starts mock-ipns + API (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`) + web (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web dev`) with `reuseExistingServer: !CI`, and `.env` files already exist locally. With the stack up (postgres 5432, kubo 5001, redis 6380, mock 3001) just run `cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test writable-shares.spec.ts --project=chromium` — the `describe.serial` block is self-contained (creates its own Alice/Bob accounts) and runs in ~1.5 min, in isolation, no flaky early tests to abort it. This directly confirmed the #555 fix (29/29) when CI couldn't.

Related: [[project-web-sdk-folder-state-desync]], [[project-web-vitest-include-test-only]], [[project-ipns-resolve-ed25519-pubkey-from-name]].

=== v1 Dockerfile
# CipherBox API - Multi-stage Docker build
# Build from repo root: docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t cipherbox-api .

# Stage 1: Install dependencies and build TypeScript
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/package.json packages/crypto/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @cipherbox/api...
COPY apps/api/ apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/ packages/crypto/
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

# Create standalone deployment (flat node_modules, no symlinks)
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api deploy /deploy --prod --legacy

# Stage 2: Production runtime
FROM node:22-alpine AS production
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -u 1001 -G appgroup
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /deploy/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/apps/api/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /deploy/package.json ./package.json

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

=== v1 run-migrations
/**
 * Programmatic migration runner for Docker containers.
 *
 * The TypeORM CLI (via ts-node) is not available in production images.
 * This script runs migrations using compiled JS entities and migrations.
 *
 * Usage (inside Docker container):
 *   node dist/run-migrations.js
 */
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { config } from 'dotenv';

config();

const dataSource = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres',
  host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
  port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432', 10),
  username: process.env.DB_USERNAME || 'postgres',
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || 'postgres',
  database: process.env.DB_DATABASE || 'cipherbox',
  entities: ['dist/**/*.entity.js'],
  migrations: ['dist/migrations/*.js'],
  logging: ['error', 'migration'],
});

async function run() {
  try {
    await dataSource.initialize();
    console.log('Running migrations...');
    const migrations = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (migrations.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');
    } else {
      console.log(`Applied ${migrations.length} migration(s):`);
      for (const m of migrations) {
        console.log(`  - ${m.name}`);
      }
    }
    await dataSource.destroy();
    console.log('Migrations complete.');
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    console.error(
      'Migration failed:',
      err.name || 'UnknownError',
      err.message?.replace(/((?:host|password|user(?:name)?)=)[^\s;,]+/gi, '$1***') || ''
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

run();

# Stock Caddy ships no rate limiter, and the front's `/routing/v1` PUT publish
# leg is deliberately token-free (blueprint/api.md, Egress) — a body cap is all
# it can bound without one.
#
# Both stages are digest-pinned: this binary terminates TLS and enforces every
# egress obligation, and the same tags feed the Lint gate. The builder bakes the
# Caddy version, so `xcaddy build` takes it from there rather than repeating it
# here, where a bump could miss one of two places and mismatch the runtime base.
FROM caddy:2.11.4-builder-alpine@sha256:7bac9be4072f7c4db2ccc7350750e0705004bf02da2ac7d96b1469ca4f28bb7c AS build

# Pinned to a commit rather than v0.1.0, the newest tag: `ipv6_prefix` landed
# after it, and masking the key to a /64 outside the module means pattern-matching
# a text address, which cannot reach the network half of a compressed one.
RUN xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit@5625512f24f6f59d6f64fb3aafe5eecff0b286db

FROM caddy:2.11.4-alpine@sha256:5f5c8640aae01df9654968d946d8f1a56c497f1dd5c5cda4cf95ab7c14d58648

COPY --from=build /usr/bin/caddy /usr/bin/caddy

=== v1 Dockerfile
# CipherBox API - Multi-stage Docker build
# Build from repo root: docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t cipherbox-api .

# Stage 1: Install dependencies and build TypeScript
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/package.json packages/crypto/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @cipherbox/api...
COPY apps/api/ apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/ packages/crypto/
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

# Create standalone deployment (flat node_modules, no symlinks)
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api deploy /deploy --prod --legacy

# Stage 2: Production runtime
FROM node:22-alpine AS production
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -u 1001 -G appgroup
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /deploy/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/apps/api/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /deploy/package.json ./package.json

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

/**
 * Programmatic migration runner for Docker containers.
 *
 * The TypeORM CLI (via ts-node) is not available in production images.
 * This script runs migrations using compiled JS entities and migrations.
 *
 * Usage (inside Docker container):
 *   node dist/run-migrations.js
 */
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { config } from 'dotenv';

config();

const dataSource = new DataSource({
  type: 'postgres',
  host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
  port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432', 10),
  username: process.env.DB_USERNAME || 'postgres',
  password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || 'postgres',
  database: process.env.DB_DATABASE || 'cipherbox',
  entities: ['dist/**/*.entity.js'],
  migrations: ['dist/migrations/*.js'],
  logging: ['error', 'migration'],
});

async function run() {
  try {
    await dataSource.initialize();
    console.log('Running migrations...');
    const migrations = await dataSource.runMigrations();
    if (migrations.length === 0) {
      console.log('No pending migrations.');
    } else {
      console.log(`Applied ${migrations.length} migration(s):`);
      for (const m of migrations) {
        console.log(`  - ${m.name}`);
      }
    }
    await dataSource.destroy();
    console.log('Migrations complete.');
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    console.error(
      'Migration failed:',
      err.name || 'UnknownError',
      err.message?.replace(/((?:host|password|user(?:name)?)=)[^\s;,]+/gi, '$1***') || ''
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

run();

import { SwaggerModule } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { buildOpenApiDocument, configureApp, corsOptionsFromEnv } from './app-setup';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap(): Promise<void> {
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' || !process.env.NODE_ENV;

    logger: isDev ? ['log', 'error', 'warn', 'debug', 'verbose'] : ['log', 'error', 'warn'],

  const document = buildOpenApiDocument(app);
  SwaggerModule.setup('api-docs', app, document, { jsonDocumentUrl: 'api-docs/json' });

  const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);
  await app.listen(port);
  logger.log(`CipherBox API listening on http://localhost:${port}`);
}

# The API area of the PR gate (blueprint/testing.md): everything that reads
# `apps/api`. Called by ci.yml. The live contract suite stays in the caller —
# it spans the Rust client and the TypeScript API and belongs to neither area.
name: CI API

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ts:
        description: The TypeScript path filter matched.
        required: true
        type: boolean

permissions: {}

jobs:
  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck (TypeScript)
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the type checker
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api typecheck

  unit:
    name: Unit tests
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the API unit suite
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test

  # The first-class API integration suite (blueprint/testing.md law 1): the
  # real-Postgres concurrency and interleaving tests — registry
  # register-vs-retire phantom and duplicate-insert, mailbox pending-cap, and
  # the advisory-lock lock_timeout DoS guard. They are named `*.itest.ts`; this
  # job owns them. Each test provisions its own randomized throwaway database
  # and drops only that one.
  integration:
    name: Integration tests (real Postgres)
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
      NODE_ENV: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0977fd99725f1db4007ccb2928dbb4e90d06cc86 # v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run the API integration suite
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test:integration

  migration-drift:
    name: Migration drift
    if: inputs.ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test

changes:
    name: Detect Changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      ts: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.ts }}
      rust: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rust }}
      web: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.web }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.e2e }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.desktop }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            ts:
              - 'apps/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              # The TS suite pins MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES against this manifest, so a
              # Rust-side chunk-size change must run it.
...
  api:
    name: API
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.ts == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-api.yml
    with:
      ts: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.ts == 'true' }}

  api-result:
    name: API Result
    needs: [changes, api]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Require the API area to pass or be skipped
        env:
          CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          AREA_RESULT: ${{ needs.api.result }}
        run: |
          echo "changes result: ${CHANGES_RESULT}; api result: ${AREA_RESULT}"
          if [ "${CHANGES_RESULT}" != 'success' ]; then
            echo "::error::change detection ${CHANGES_RESULT}, so the API area never ran"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${AREA_RESULT}" = 'failure' ] || [ "${AREA_RESULT}" = 'cancelled' ]; then
            echo "::error::the API area ${AREA_RESULT}"
            exit 1
          fi

import dataSource from './data-source';

async function run(): Promise<void> {

The v2 scaffold removed `apps/api/Dockerfile` and the compiled migration runner. `deploy-staging.yml` still builds the one and runs the other, so the WIP dispatch path that the cutover uses could not complete. The last staging deploy is the v1 one from 2026-03.

- mattpocock-skills:code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- mattpocock-skills:resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- mattpocock-skills:wizard: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
- mattpocock-skills:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

There still is. The tag path is intact, but it cannot run yet.

- `tag-staging.yml` is the staging release path: manual dispatch, then it asserts a `vX.Y.Z` release tag on the `main` HEAD, runs the full web and desktop e2e suites, waits on the `staging-approval` environment, mints a `staging-*` tag, and that tag fires `deploy-staging.yml`.
- The assertion is the block today. No v2 release tag exists. Release PR #1758 mints `v2.0.0` when it merges, and the release order holds that merge until after the cutover.
- So the first v2 deploy goes through the `workflow_dispatch` path of `deploy-staging.yml` at a `main` SHA. The blueprint names that path for WIP v2 deploys before the first release, and the #653 gate asks for it to run once.

After the cutover: merge #1758, `v2.0.0` gets tagged, and from then every staging deploy goes through `tag-staging.yml`. The same `deploy-staging.yml` runs at the end of both paths, so the image, the migration runner, and the wipe step are shared.

content.text:
The wipe step is in `deploy-staging.yml` because that is the one workflow that reaches the VPS. There is no separate cutover workflow.

- The step is gated. It runs only when `wipe_volumes` is true, and that input exists only on the `workflow_dispatch` trigger. A `staging-*` tag push cannot set it, and a `workflow_call` from `tag-staging.yml` cannot pass it. So the tag path never wipes.
- The default is false. A plain dispatch without the flag is a normal deploy over the existing volumes.
- The blueprint's law 3 sets the design: staging is destructive-restorable, and a deploy may always be "fresh volumes, redeploy, done". The cutover is a redeploy with that one flag, not a separate procedure. #1388 added the flag for that reason.

So the step is the cutover switch inside the normal deploy. After the cutover it stays as the reset button for staging: one dispatch with the flag gives a fresh stack.

=== api.md 195-240
  recursive: every block is uploaded and registered individually, and a recursive
  pin would make repo GC walk sealed bytes it cannot interpret.
- **Egress**: the API process serves no bytes. CipherBox runs a Kubo-backed
  **trustless gateway** (block/CAR responses, client-side CID verification)
  gated by the read accelerator token above — never the session JWT, which would
  put full API authority on the system's highest-frequency credential
  presentation (roughly one per leaf block). Any public trustless gateway is the
  no-auth fallback; reads survive CipherBox infra loss.
- **The front covers both read legs.** One `forward_auth` front sits in front of
  Kubo's gateway leg and someguy's `/routing/v1` GET/resolve leg, gating both on
  the same pseudonym — reads present it, writes never do, and the gate admits
  only `GET` and `HEAD` so a read credential cannot turn into a write against an
  accelerator that would have taken one. The `/routing/v1`
  **PUT** publish leg stays open: an IPNS record carries its own signature, so
  the front has nothing to add there beyond IP-keyed rate limiting. The
  republisher's re-PUTs route internally and never traverse the front.
- **What the `forward_auth` front owes the pseudonym.** Five requirements, all
  load-bearing: deny on **any** non-204, not only 401, so a verify-side fault
  fails closed; never log the `Authorization` header, since the raw pseudonym in
  a proxy access log is a gateway credential at rest; **strip** it before
  proxying upstream, so it does not reach Kubo's or someguy's logs either; and
  name **nothing about what is being read** on the verify subrequest — the API's
  view of a read is a bare "is this session alive", and a forwarded request path
  would make it account + CID, or account + IPNS name, on every read. Not
  logging client IPs belongs here too: the pseudonym removes the account from
  the gateway tier, but an IP recorded beside a read re-links it — and that
  applies to the accelerators' own logs, which ship offsite, so the client
  address is stripped alongside the pseudonym on every leg into Kubo or someguy —
  in `X-Forwarded-For` and in the whole `CF-*` family Cloudflare adds beside it,
  `CF-Ray` above all, since that is the id under which Cloudflare's own logs
  record the requested path and would join a pseudonym at the verify leg to a CID
  at the accelerator. The one place the front forwards the address is the verify
  subrequest, so that surface's rate limit bounds a member rather than the front;
  `Range` and `Accept` are stripped there, since the byte window and the
  block-vs-CAR shape describe the read as surely as its path would.
- **What the verify leg costs.** The API is told, per read, that this session is
  alive and which address asked — no CID and no name. It already sees that
  address on every other route the same member calls, so the pairing is not new;
  what is new is the **cadence**, roughly one presentation per leaf block, which
  is read timing, session duration, and approximate volume per account. The
  in-process cache does not blunt it: the request still arrives. This is the
  price of the unlinkability claim, not a hole in it — the claim is scoped to a
  gateway-tier observer, and the API necessarily resolves pseudonym to account
  at verify time.
  Media streaming uses ranged block/CAR fetches through the existing
  service-worker decryption layer.

=== TS seam type
/** A capped record GET: the stored bytes, `null` for absence, or over-cap. */
export type CappedRecordResult = { kind: 'record'; record: Uint8Array | null } | TooLargeResult;

/**
 * Dumb `/routing/v1` byte mover: GET/PUT of opaque signed record bytes.
 *
 * The endpoint set includes untrusted public endpoints, so `getRecord` bounds
 * the read at `maxBytes` as the body arrives (see `cappedBody.ts`).
 */
export interface RecordTransportSeam {
  endpoints(): string[];
  getRecord(endpoint: string, routingKey: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<CappedRecordResult>;
  putRecord(endpoint: string, routingKey: string, record: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;
}

/** One HTTP request fully described by the engine. */
export interface HttpRequestData {
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE' | 'HEAD';
  url: string;
  headers: Array<[string, string]>;
  body: Uint8Array | null;
  /**
   * Ambient-credential scope. Absent means `'omit'`: only the API origin is
   * asked for the HTTP-only refresh cookie, so a gateway gets no authority it
   * could use to correlate the per-leaf fetches.
   */
  credentials?: 'include' | 'omit';
  /** Whole-request deadline in ms, per request class; absent leaves it unbounded. */
  timeoutMs?: number | null;
}

/** One HTTP response, returned verbatim to the engine. */
export interface HttpResponseData {
  status: number;
  headers: Array<[string, string]>;
  body: Uint8Array;

=== deploy.md 176-200
Caddy enforces membership; Kubo serves. Token format and TTL are API
build-time detail. Public trustless gateways remain the no-auth fallback,
so this path can fail without breaking reads.

Two vhosts, `gateway-staging` and `routing-staging`, both under the origin
certificate the other vhosts use — so a new hostname needs its SAN and a DNS
record before it resolves. Which legs are gated, and what the front owes the
pseudonym, is api.md (Egress); because neither vhost logs, those obligations
are asserted against Caddy's adapted config in the **Lint** gate rather than
read out of the Caddyfile. `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` must equal the number of
`X-Forwarded-For` entries that actually reach the API, not the number of boxes
in front of it. Caddy is given Cloudflare's published ranges as
`trusted_proxies`, so it keeps the member address Cloudflare appended and adds
its own beside it: two entries arrive and the count is 2. The two settings are
one unit — trust without the count keys every IP-keyed limit on Cloudflare's
edge, the count without the trust runs off the end of the header onto an entry
the caller wrote — so the same **Lint** gate holds them to each other.

`{client_ip}` reads **`CF-Connecting-IP`** under `trusted_proxies_strict`, not
`X-Forwarded-For`. Cloudflare _appends_ to the latter, so every entry left of the
caller's own is caller-written, and strict mode walks past trusted ranges to the
first entry outside them — which for a caller whose own address sits inside a
Cloudflare range (a Worker, WARP, a Tunnel) is an entry it wrote. Cloudflare
writes and overwrites `CF-Connecting-IP` itself, so it has no prepend surface;
strict still refuses both headers from an untrusted peer, so a direct-to-origin

- The CipherBox routing accelerator is one named source that presents the session pseudonym (`Authorization: Bearer …`) on GET. Public routing endpoints never get the header. PUT never carries it on any endpoint (writes never present the pseudonym; the front takes only GET and HEAD through the gate).

Two options: (a) the engine passes an `Option` bearer into `get_record` for the accelerator endpoint, and the TS transport sets the header when given; or (b) the engine hands the TS transport a request description like the `Http` seam does. Pick the smaller change that keeps the pseudonym out of any public endpoint by construction, and state the reason in the PR body. - Config: add a routing accelerator URL beside the public endpoint list, the same way `acceleratorBaseUrl` sits beside `publicGateways` in `packages/client/src/spawnEngineWorker.ts` and `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts`. No. I meant a second `workflow_dispatch` of `deploy-staging.yml` at the `main` SHA, without the wipe flag. That path stays valid before the first release exists.

The tag path is the other option, and it is the better one now:

- Merge #1758. That mints `v2.0.0` on `main`.
- Dispatch `tag-staging.yml`. It asserts the release tag, runs the full web and desktop e2e suites, waits on the `staging-approval` environment, mints the `staging-*` tag, and that tag runs the same `deploy-staging.yml` without a wipe.

The order matters: the #1808 fix must merge before #1758, so the `v2.0.0` tag contains it. Release-please rebases its PR on every push to `main`, so the fix lands in the release commit by itself.

The release order was "cutover, then #1758". The cutover ran, so #1758 is free to merge once #1808 is in. That makes the first tag-staging deploy the one that ships the fix, and the WIP dispatch path is not needed again.

So: #1808 merges, I set the new routing accelerator variable on the `staging` environment, you merge #1758, then you dispatch `tag-staging.yml` and approve at the `staging-approval` gate.

## Verdict

The core splice is sound. The credential cannot reach a public endpoint, a PUT, or a cleartext hop, and a refused gated leg is never read as a vacancy. Findings below are about the configuration edge, the missing Rust-side conformance coverage, and one deployment hazard.

## Findings

1. **SHOULD FIX — the config edge now accepts an accelerator-only record plane, collapsing the endpoint set to one operator.**
   `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts:119`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/engine/config.rs:86`, mirrored by `packages/client/src/seams/recordTransport.ts:58` and `crates/desktop-seams/src/record_transport.rs:67`.
   The old guard demanded at least one routing endpoint; the new one is satisfied by the accelerator alone. In the web path `list(env.VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS ?? DEFAULT)` uses `??`, so a GitHub repo variable that is merely *unset* arrives as `''` (not `undefined`), yields `[]`, and no longer fails the build once `VITE_ROUTING_ACCELERATOR_URL` is set — one forgotten staging variable silently ships a plane whose only endpoint is CipherBox's. That breaks `blueprint/engine.md:86` ("someguy plus at least one independent endpoint") and hands one operator the `FanoutRecord::Absent` unanimity vote its own doc comment warns about. The concrete consequence is in `crates/engine/src/net/provision.rs:95` — `require_vacant_vault_pointer` reaches `Ok(())` on a unanimous "no record", and the mint that follows overwrites the one record naming the root. Fix: require at least one endpoint that is not the accelerator (or, minimally, keep the "must list at least one routing endpoint" refusal and let the accelerator only *join* a non-empty set), in both config edges and both transports.

2. **SHOULD FIX — no Rust-side test holds a host transport to the bearer contract.**
   `crates/engine/src/testkit/conformance/record_transport.rs:33,53,68` pass `None` for every case, and `crates/desktop-seams/tests/conformance.rs` has no equivalent of the three TypeScript tests added in `packages/client/src/seams/recordTransport.test.ts`. Nothing in a merge gate would catch `ReqwestRecordTransport` dropping the header (silent 403s in staging only) or a later edit adding `Authorization` to `put_record` — the rule that a read pseudonym never authorizes a write would then be enforced by a comment alone. Fix: extend the shared conformance kit with "presents the given bearer on GET, sends none when given none, never sends one on PUT", so both host transports are held to it.

3. **SHOULD FIX — the `Authorization` header makes every browser record GET a preflighted request, and the front admits only GET and HEAD.**
   `packages/client/src/seams/recordTransport.ts:83-91` with `blueprint/api.md` ("the gate admits only `GET` and `HEAD`"). `Authorization` is not CORS-safelisted, so the web client now issues an `OPTIONS` preflight to the gated `/routing/v1` leg; if the `forward_auth` front denies or does not answer `OPTIONS` with `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization`, every accelerator read from a tab fails. It degrades safely (transport error → `Unavailable`, other endpoints still answer) — but combined with finding 1 it is a total read outage, and no CI job exercises it (`web-e2e.yml` and `desktop-e2e.yml` both leave the variable unset by design). Fix: confirm the front answers the preflight before the staging variable is set, and say so where the variable is documented.

4. **INFORMATIONAL — the pseudonym becomes an unzeroizable copy on both host paths.**
   `crates/wasm/src/seams_bridge.rs:476` converts it to an owned `String` and then to an immutable JS string that only GC reclaims; `bearer_header` (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:53`) builds `format!("Bearer {token}")` into a plain `String`. The engine-side `Zeroizing<String>` from `read_credential` is therefore the only buffer actually wiped. This is the same shape the existing `Http` seam already has for the API bearer, so it is not a new class, and the credential is read-scoped and rotates on refresh. No change recommended beyond not widening it.

5. **INFORMATIONAL — the desktop transport does not percent-encode the routing key, the browser one does.**

Every live caller passes `IpnsName::as_str()` (base36, from a public key), so nothing today is injectable, and the scheme+authority prefix means no crafted key can move the request to another host. Now that this GET carries a credential, matching the encoding removes the asymmetry cheaply.

6. **INFORMATIONAL — a non-https accelerator degrades silently.**
   `crates/engine/src/net/record_accelerator.rs:31` correctly refuses to arm a URL failing `carries_credentials_safely`, but the endpoint stays in the fan-out set and simply reads unauthenticated, with nothing surfaced. A staging deploy mistyping `http://` would look healthy while the gated leg 403s everything. Consider refusing a non-https `VITE_ROUTING_ACCELERATOR_URL` at the config edge (as `apiBaseUrl` already does for the API origin) so the mistake is loud at build time.

A trailing-slash difference between `VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS` and `VITE_ROUTING_ACCELERATOR_URL` yields two entries for the same host, one of them unarmed — a duplicate request and a confusing half-authenticated plane, not a credential leak (the spelling that is not armed is shown nothing).

- **Endpoint confusion:** `read_credential` compares against `armed` by exact `EndpointId` equality and is *not* delegated to the inner seam, so a host implementation cannot arm an endpoint of its own; every non-test read path (`fanout.rs:147`, `provision.rs:117`) pairs the credential with the same endpoint it hands to `get_record`.

- **PUT:** `put_record` takes no bearer anywhere in the trait, both transports, or the WASM bridge.
- **Attacker-controlled 403:** a refusal is `Err(_) → continue` in `fanout_get_classified`, never a `vacant` vote, so `Absent` is unreachable while the gated leg refuses; covered by `a_refused_accelerator_beside_an_absent_public_answer_stays_unavailable`. `require_vacant_vault_pointer` returns `Indeterminate` on the same input.
- **Leakage:** no error string or `Debug` impl on either path carries the token; `SeamError::new("record_transport get: bearer is unusable")` is field-less.

PR #1809 is up for #1808. CI is green on all 39 checks, and the CodeRabbit verdict is still pending. I watch for it in the background.

**What the PR does**

- The host transport names its accelerator. The engine wraps the seam once, and that wrapper alone fills the pseudonym for the armed endpoint on GET. No call site can pick the endpoint that sees the credential. PUT takes no credential at all.
- New variable `VITE_ROUTING_ACCELERATOR_URL` names the gated CipherBox endpoint. `VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS` keeps its meaning as the public list and stays mandatory, so one operator never holds the whole record plane. The desktop shell gets the same surface.
- Four new engine tests pin the header placement and the unavailable verdict. One desktop transport test and the client suite cover the TS side.
- The three review passes ran. The findings are folded in, and three are rejected with reasons in the PR body.

**Done on the staging side.** `VITE_ROUTING_ACCELERATOR_URL` is set on the `staging` environment. The gated leg's preflight answers 204 with `Authorization` in the allowed headers, so the browser's request goes through.

**Your steps, in order**

1. Merge #1809 after the CodeRabbit verdict. I report it when it lands.
2. Merge #1758. That mints `v2.0.0` with the fix inside.
3. Dispatch `tag-staging.yml` and approve at the `staging-approval` gate. That deploy has no wipe.
4. Sign in on `app-staging`.

- [WAVE 18 + SMOKE-TEST TAIL 2026-09-06 — 41 merges; ADR 0018 ACCEPTED; #1805 merged 2026-09-13; V2 CUTOVER DONE 2026-09-13 19:13Z (run 34776866429); AOP ARMED, #1507 closed; Grafana stack DOWN; STAGING SIGN-IN BROKEN → #1808 (routing resolve leg needs the pseudonym), lane running; tag-staging.yml is the deploy path after #1758](project-wave18-state.md) — 4 post-cutover follow-ups filed; log in scratchpad wave18-plan.md
- [WAVE 17 QUEUE EMPTY 2026-09-03 — 58 merges, 103 closes, open v2.0.0 126→70](project-wave17-state.md) — wave close pending: user decisions #1663 #1667 #1670 #1697 #1692, HITL walks, orphan sweep, wave 18 plan; log inside
- [WAVE 16 CLOSED 2026-08-31 — 16 PRs, 140→126 open](project-wave16-state.md) — L4b/P4/tail never launched → wave 17; 11 orphan slices to parent
- [WAVE 15 CLOSED 2026-08-26 — 16 PRs, ~43 closes, 167→140 open](project-wave15-state.md) — replay-starvation fix in the final PR; lessons inside
- [WAVE 14 APPROVED 2026-08-24](project-wave14-state.md) — #858 layered erase + #1244 opaque pseudonym DECIDED; agenda left: #1268, #953
- [Wave-14 decomposition FILED — 31 issues #1370-#1400](project-wave14-decomposition-filed.md) — 13 decisions settled+durable; do not re-decompose
- [WAVE 13 LAUNCHED 2026-08-20](project-wave13-state.md) — 4 decisions recorded; undecomposed-umbrella flag inside
- Closed waves: [12](project-wave12-state.md), [10](project-wave10-state.md) (mutation testing caught vacuous guards), [8](project-wave8-state.md), [7](project-wave7-planning-state.md), [6](project-wave6-closed.md) ("trust an unsigned field" ×3), [4](project-wave4-review-queue-state.md) (`recycle-both.sh`; `git merge-file` sim before 2nd same-field PR merges) — lesson hooks inside each file
- [v2 build tracker is LIVE](project-v2-build-tracker.md) — umbrella #655, milestone v2.0.0; work from tracker, don't re-plan
- [Blueprint corrections need the FULL ADR process](feedback-blueprint-corrections-need-adr.md) — draft in cipher-box-next, user accepts, THEN reword the blueprint
- [Sub-issue tree COMPLETE](project-umbrella-sub-issue-tree-conversion.md); [wayfinder map COMPLETE](project-cipher-box-next-wayfinder-map.md); [ADRs live in cipher-box-next `decisions/`](project-adrs-live-in-cipher-box-next-decisions.md) — `docs/adr/` is dead v1 residue
- [v1 is staging-only, all-DEVNET](project-v1-staging-only-devnet.md) — no prod; latent prod Web3Auth configs not a bug
- [Identity plane: TS reconstructs key, Rust derives](project-v2-identity-plane-ts-reconstructs-key.md) — web3auth stays TS
- [/simplify + /security-review MANDATORY per draft PR](feedback-simplify-security-review-mandatory-per-draft-pr.md) — +crypto-privacy if crypto; brief EVERY ship agent
- [Implement small in-scope changes, don't defer](feedback-implement-small-changes-dont-defer.md) — implement-now > fold into OPEN issue > new issue
- [STANDING: implement follow-ups IN the wave](feedback-implement-followups-in-wave.md) — waves must DECREASE the issue count; FILING BAR for cycle briefs (fold > comment on open issue > new issue only for a real defect) after the 26-vs-7 night of 2026-09-03
- [STANDING: v2.0.0 filing bar + burndown wave 16](feedback-v2-filing-bar-and-burndown.md) — `post-cutover` milestone exists; brief every agent
- [No absence-justifying comments](feedback-no-absence-justifying-comments.md) and [comments short, no workaround apologia](feedback-comments-short-no-workaround-apologia.md) — rationale once, at its home; both in AGENTS.md

## Commit Hooks / Git Signing / Bg Agents

- lint-staged: markdownlint+prettier on `.md`, eslint on `.ts/.tsx`; MD036 no bold heading, MD031/032 blank lines around fences+lists. Tell md sub-agents. commitlint local hook skipped → CI enforces.
- [Automated commits bypass pre-commit lint](project-automated-commits-bypass-precommit-lint.md) — CI `eslint .` backstop
- [Entire does not capture subagent traces](project-entire-subagent-trace-capture-gap.md) — commit in-tree artifacts
- [Branch switch drops tracked scripts](project-branch-switch-drops-tracked-scripts.md) — `git checkout HEAD -- scripts/`
- [CI/release work uses chore(ci) not fix](feedback-ci-release-work-uses-chore-ci.md)
- [1Password SSH signing hangs](project-1password-ssh-signing-hangs.md) — never `--no-gpg-sign`; `timeout`-guard. [gsd commit helper false negative](project-gsd-commit-helper-false-negative.md) — verify git log, don't retry
- [Resume background worktree agents](project-resume-background-worktree-agents.md) — pause=TaskStop, resume via FRESH agent. [Lost-wake + evicted transcript](project-bg-executor-lost-wake-continuation.md) — verify from disk; `| tee` masks exit codes

- [CR CLI cooldown must be waited INLINE](feedback-cr-cli-cooldown-inline-not-detached.md) — detached sleep = silent lost-wake
- [Sandbox REFUSES foreground `sleep` → agents stop short](project-sandbox-refuses-foreground-sleep-agents-stop-short.md) — wait via a polling SCRIPT as a foreground Bash call (timeout 540000); resume via SendMessage

- [Web-e2e local full-suite recipe](project-web-e2e-local-full-suite-recipe.md). [sdk-e2e from a worktree](project-sdk-e2e-worktree-live-checkpoint-run.md) — copy `.env`

- [Leave the docker stack running after ship/e2e](feedback-leave-docker-stack-running.md)
- [API dev must start FROM apps/api](project-api-dev-must-start-from-apps-api.md) — from the root it skips .env; uploads 503, cold start never settles

## Issue Hygiene / Sub-Agent Orchestration

- [Follow-ups → GitHub issues THIS SPRINT](feedback-todos-go-to-gsd-capture-not-github-issues.md) — label v2-build

- [AskUserQuestion: don't skip after an interrupt](feedback-dont-skip-askuserquestion-after-interrupt.md), [BROKEN on mobile](feedback-askuserquestion-broken-on-mobile.md), [lead with per-option pros/cons](feedback-lead-with-pros-cons-before-asking.md), [decision questions in PLAIN WORDS, no engine jargon](feedback-decision-questions-in-plain-words.md)

- [STE-100 prose clause in EVERY sub-agent brief](feedback-ste100-in-all-subagent-briefs.md) — issues/PR bodies/comments/reports; code+quotes exempt
- [Every filed issue carries ONE comp:* label](feedback-comp-label-required-on-filed-issues.md) — board groups by it; add at filing time, name it in every brief

=== workflow
# v2 release management (blueprint/deploy.md in FSM1/cipher-box-next): one
# product version vX.Y.Z, single-component release-please, no per-package
# versioning. Every push to main updates one release PR; merging it mints the
# `vX.Y.Z` tag that desktop-release.yml and tag-staging.yml key on.
name: Release Please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

# One release PR. Two merges close together would otherwise race the action
# into two states of the same PR.
concurrency:
  group: release-please
  cancel-in-progress: false

# The App token carries the write scopes, and it also makes the release PR
# push trigger CI, which a job-token push does not. No step reads the job
# token, so it gets nothing.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      releases_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.releases_created }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ vars.RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@45996ed1f6d02564a971a2fa1b5860e934307cf7 # v5.0.0
        id: release
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Release summary
        if: steps.release.outputs.releases_created == 'true'
        env:
          RELEASES_OUTPUT: ${{ toJSON(steps.release.outputs) }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "## Releases Created"
            echo '```json'
            echo "$RELEASES_OUTPUT" | jq '{releases_created, paths_released}'
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# v2 release management (blueprint/deploy.md in FSM1/cipher-box-next): one
# product version vX.Y.Z, single-component release-please, no per-package
# versioning. Every push to main updates one release PR; merging it mints the
# `vX.Y.Z` tag that desktop-release.yml and tag-staging.yml key on.
name: Release Please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

# One release PR. Two merges close together would otherwise race the action
# into two states of the same PR.
concurrency:
  group: release-please
  cancel-in-progress: false

# The App token carries the write scopes, and it also makes the release PR
# push trigger CI, which a job-token push does not. No step reads the job
# token, so it gets nothing.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      releases_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.releases_created }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ vars.RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@45996ed1f6d02564a971a2fa1b5860e934307cf7 # v5.0.0
        id: release
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Release summary
        if: steps.release.outputs.releases_created == 'true'
        env:
          RELEASES_OUTPUT: ${{ toJSON(steps.release.outputs) }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "## Releases Created"
            echo '```json'
            echo "$RELEASES_OUTPUT" | jq '{releases_created, paths_released}'
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

### Release-tag gating (the v1 shape, simplified)

`tag-staging.yml` ports with its chain intact — it was the part of v1
release management that worked:

1. `workflow_dispatch` → assert `main` HEAD carries a `v*` tag (one regex,
   replacing v1's three-pattern component zoo). Untagged HEAD fails with
   "wait for release-please".
2. Re-run the e2e gates at that SHA via the reusable workflows — web,
   desktop mounted, and (new) the cross-client suite. This is the
   release-tag e2e gating testing.md handed here: the main gate already ran
   revert-first at merge time; this re-run is the deploy-time assertion
   that HEAD is still green, on the exact bits being shipped.
3. `staging-approval` environment gate (manual approval) → mint
   `staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N` → call `deploy-staging.yml`.
